mission.brief: Display the LF count, word count and UTF-8 byte count for note.txt with the appropriate wc option. The final record lacks LF. Non-ASCII characters occupy multiple bytes. Show all three counts.
constraints: Only simulated UTF-8 text. No host shell, files, processes or network.
Use Command reference for the exact supported subset; no regex, globbing, variables, escapes or unsupported options. Quotes group literal words.
Locale is C: bytewise sorting and ASCII word separators. wc -c counts UTF-8 bytes; wc -l counts LF characters.
Inspection goals require the named tool and exact displayed result from the relevant source; equivalent supported paths and approaches count.
Only declared report destinations may be written. > truncates before input is read; errors do not undo writes. >> appends.
Any actual write clears earlier verification. Finish changes before inspecting the final outputs. Final report grading does not require one exact transcript.

hints: Different counting questions need different options; a visually plausible number is insufficient.
The last record has no newline; accented and CJK text uses multiple bytes.
Use wc -l, wc -w and wc -c on note.txt.

lesson.goal: Display the LF count, word count and UTF-8 byte count for note.txt with the appropriate wc option. The final record lacks LF. Non-ASCII characters occupy multiple bytes. Show all three counts.

steps.explanation: -l counts LF characters, not every displayed record. The unterminated last record adds no LF.
-w counts groups separated by ASCII whitespace in this C-locale subset.
-c counts encoded bytes, not Unicode characters. café and 猫 demonstrate the distinction.
